Key West: 205 Whitehead St..place: 205 Whitehead St, Key West, FL 33040, USA
Key West: 205 Whitehead St..standpoint: Standing in the street facing north east
Key West: 205 Whitehead St..subject: two-storey Key West wood-frame Conch house
Key West: 205 Whitehead St..layout: Centrally situated historic two-storey Key West wood-frame Conch house with a plumb rectangular massing and a pitched side-gable roof featuring two symmetrical triangular dormers. Exterior cladding consists of weathered, chalking off-white horizontal timber clapboards showing minor paint peeling and micro-cracking across exposed elevations. Ground level features an integrated colonnaded veranda supported by plain, plumb square timber posts; upper level exhibits recessed framed openings aligned symmetrically. The roof is clad in dull silver-gray standing-seam metal panels with localized dark patina and mildew accumulation along drip edges and roof valleys. Base of the building rests slightly elevated upon rough-cut native Key Largo coral limestone piers. Adjacent to the left stands a secondary timber-clad vernacular structure painted faded pale cyan with a low-slope white metal roof. Street level consists of aggregate-exposed, medium-gray asphalt paving bordered by a weathered, light-gray poured concrete curb. Flanking and overarching the house is a dense, mature tropical canopy comprising broad, multi-stemmed Swietenia mahagoni and irregular Ficus aurea with twisting branch structures, interspersed with tall, slender Cocos nucifera trunks. Surface textures display maritime salt-film hazing, damp algae staining on recessed porch ceilings, and coarse wood-grain relief throughout.
Key West: 205 Whitehead St..focus: The foliage, species, fauna, trees, bushes, mosses, lichen, material surfaces, surface weathering in local micro climate, chemical composition and hard surface weathering.

Key West: 243 Front St..place: The Custom House, 281 Front St, Key West, FL 33040, USA
Key West: 243 Front St..standpoint: Standing in the street facing north
Key West: 243 Front St..subject: The Key West Museum of Art and History is frame left with Clinton Sq. Market beyond.
Key West: 243 Front St..layout: Deep terracotta-red brick surfaces displaying uneven charcoal-gray soiling concentrated beneath projecting eaves corbels, window heads, string courses, and the ground-floor arcade arches, constructed from smooth pressed red clay masonry in regular running bond; monumental four-storey civic building massing with a ground-level round-arched arcade, rectangular and round-arched double-hung sash windows, an upper-storey arcaded window register, and a corbelled brick cornice, capped by a steep-pitched hip and cross-gable roof clad in orange-red terra cotta tiles, punctuated by a tall rectangular brick chimney and small hip-roofed dormers. Adjacent mid-ground structure presents buff-gray to off-white weathered surfaces across lime-rendered masonry and weatherboard siding, forming a two-storey gabled warehouse sheltered by an oxidized silver-gray standing-seam sheet-metal roof showing dull white oxidation. Distant single-storey secondary structures feature flat and low-pitch corrugated metal roofs. Ground surface consists of charcoal-gray interlocking pavers laid in a herringbone pattern across the roadway, bordered by cast concrete curbs, pale gray concrete sidewalks, red-brown brick paver sections, and a low white-painted retaining wall topped with black iron picket railings. Prominent *Ficus aurea* specimen flanks the street with thick, sinuous fluted boles, multiple descending aerial roots fused into pillar trunks, and a broad, horizontally spreading heavy-limb framework, alongside compact upright *Conocarpus erectus* trunks.

Key West: 1000 Whitehead, Lighthouse.place: The Custom House, 281 Front St, Key West, FL 33040, USA
Key West: 1000 Whitehead, Lighthouse.standpoint: Standing in the street facing north
Key West: 1000 Whitehead, Lighthouse.subject: Looking down street past houses and through trees that line the street.
Key West: 1000 Whitehead, Lighthouse.layout: Subtropical residential road corridor bordered by mature dense tree canopies. Center ground composed of mid-gray asphalt with painted yellow median markings, bordered by pale gray cast concrete curbs and sidewalk paving slabs. Rising behind perimeter boundaries, a tapered conical lighthouse tower finished in uniform bright white paint over brick masonry, capped by a dark-painted metal gallery railing and glazed lantern room. Flanking road margins enclosed by smooth bright white-painted rendered masonry perimeter walls inset with dark metal railings between square piers, alongside white-painted timber picket fences and black-painted cast-metal decorative lampposts with bracketed lanterns. Recessed behind foliage, two-storey vernacular timber structures finished in crisp white-painted horizontal clapboard siding, featuring stacked double-tier covered verandas with square timber posts, railings, and pale gray standing-seam sheet metal roofs without dormers. Flanking streetscape heavily dominated by massive *Ficus aurea* with dense networks of aerial roots and muscular woody boughs, broad umbrella-like branching of mature *Delonix regia*, and tall, slender ringed trunks of *Sabal palmetto* punctuating upper levels. Planar wall geometries rectified plumb to gravity vertical, window fenestration aligned in uniform grids, with dense foliage forming a continuous vaulted overhead canopy over the road axis. Surface finishes exhibit maintained paintwork with faint biological patination throughout.

Key West: The Palms Hotel.place: 819 White St, Key West, FL 33040, USA
Key West: The Palms Hotel.standpoint: Standing in the street looking directly at The Palms Hotel.
Key West: The Palms Hotel.subject: The center of the frame is dominated with The Palms Hotel.
Key West: The Palms Hotel.layout: The Victorian houses, now a hotel, is seen veiled by 17 tall narrow palms with a flowered hedge and garden bed abutting the sidewalk in the shallow front yard. Architectural Style and Features Original Construction: Designed as two separate residential mansions (at 820 and 822 White St.) for the prominent Williams family during the late-19th-century Gilded Age. Classic Key West / Victorian Influences: It embodies the quintessential "Old Key West" residential design, featuring traditional wooden-frame construction typical of historic island homes built by local shipbuilders and master carpenters. Facade and Balconies: Features a classic white facade, traditional covered porches and balconies with white railings, and architectural detailing overseen and protected by the local Historical Architectural Review Commission. Outdoor Layout: The structures are arranged to overlook a lush, secluded tropical garden courtyard and a heated outdoor swimming pool, blending indoor-outdoor living spaces characteristic of the Florida Keys Evolution: After serving various roles through the 20th century—including as a boarding house and apartments in the 1970s and 1980s—the buildings were consolidated and restored in 1993 into the boutique hotel layout seen today while preserving their original Victorian-era proportions and charm.
Key West: The Palms Hotel.weather: Hurricane, Dark Skies, Rain, Flooding, Powerful Sustained Wind
